title: Repeating Work
goal: The three looping keywords, and how to leave a loop.

sections.text: Rust has three looping keywords, and they behave much like the ones you already know from other languages.
`while` repeats as long as its condition holds. `for` walks over a range or a collection. `loop` repeats forever.

sections.caption: Three keywords, three shapes of repetition.

sections.text: `break` leaves the loop immediately. `continue` skips the rest of this turn and starts the next one. Both work in all three kinds of loop.

One thing is different from most languages. A `break` inside `loop` can carry a value out, and that value becomes the result of the loop. This makes `loop` the natural choice when you are searching for something.

sections.caption: break carries the answer out of the loop.

sections.text: A range like `1..5` counts from 1 up to but not including 5. Write `1..=5` when you want the last number included.
